chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Give to the beggar, even if he is upon the back of a horse.'

key_terms.فَرَس: Horse, used here as a symbol of wealth or status

ai.seo_question: What should one do if a beggar appears wealthy or dignified?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes the virtue of generosity by instructing believers to give to the supplicant even if they appear dignified or wealthy, symbolized by being on a horse. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly principle of not judging the sincerity of charity by outward status, thereby preventing the repulsion of the beggar and encouraging consistent almsgiving regardless of social perception.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give to the beggar, and even though he may be upon a horse (looks financially in sound position)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “
Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’You must give charity to one asking for help even if he is riding a horse.’”
